title: Mastery of Ocular Local Anaesthesia: A Clinical Compendium
summary: A comprehensive guide to the pharmacodynamics, delivery techniques, and safety protocols for regional anaesthesia in ophthalmic surgery. Essential for residents and fellows mastering peri-bulbar, retro-bulbar, and topical modalities.

sections.title: Red Flags: Retrobulbar/Peribulbar Block
content: Globe perforation (myopic eyes at highest risk)
Retrobulbar hemorrhage (symptoms: rapid proptosis, elevated IOP, pain)

content.explanation: Depth of pressure (too much), Duration (sustained), Direct contact (nerve stimulation), Dose (too much anaesthetic), Diagnosis (hypoxia/hypercarbia exacerbation).

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Always aspirate before injection to avoid intravascular delivery.
In patients on anticoagulation, consider topical or sub-tenon to avoid retrobulbar hemorrhage.
Hyaluronidase (15-50 IU/ml) is used to improve the diffusion of the anaesthetic.
Max dose of lidocaine is 3-5mg/kg (with epinephrine up to 7mg/kg).
Monitor pulse oximetry and ECG during regional blocks.

sections.title: Contraindications
content: Local infection at site of injection
Known allergy to amide or ester type anaesthetics
